text:
anya: quick question — thinking about a small RFC follow-up: can we add a lightweight per-shard 'fast-open' header that includes: format, shard-size, chunk-count, and an optional chunk-level checksum table to enable safe streaming-warmup without a full manifest?

sam: curious, what's the main goal vs just keeping the manifest? is this for cold-start bandwidth or for safety?

anya: both. use cases: 1) avoid an extra manifest fetch roundtrip for tiny probes, 2) allow early KV-cache warmup while we stream weights, 3) verify chunks on the fly so we can evict/rollback if checksum mismatch.

mike: +1 for streaming safety. but worry: adding chunk checksums in the header could bloat the header and defeat the 'lightweight' goal. how many chunks are we expecting per shard?

anya: typical shard ~200MB split into 64KB chunks -> ~3200 checksums, so yeah header would be huge if inline. idea: header can contain either a checksum-table-hash (content-address pointer) or inline small tables for tiny shards.

tara: what about a sidecar index approach? content-addressed index blob stored next to the shard (shard.cksum). Clients can try header->fast path; if header only has index-hash, they can fetch index as needed in parallel with weight stream. keeps header small.

sam: that feels similar to manifestless designs we've debated before. main tradeoff is the extra fetch (index) vs trust model if we don't verify. If index is fetched in parallel it may add a latency hit but we can proceed with streaming and mark segments 'unverified' until index arrives. fallback behavior?

anya: fallback rules proposal: - if header has inline table -> verify as you stream. - if header has index-hash -> start streaming, warmup prefix into KV cache as verified=false, compute local rolling checksums; once index fetched, compare and either promote verified or trigger eviction/rollback for mismatched ranges. - if verification fails, fall back to model-variant or local cached weight.

mike: eviction/rollback on mismatch is expensive. Do we have safe partial-rollback semantics? what about in-flight requests using the KV cache?

tara: suggest a 'verification tombstone' mark in KV cache API: warmup entries marked provisional; runtime rejects cache hits that are provisional for end-to-end correctness unless request is at low-latency tolerance. That plus a GC/rollback job that atomically unpins provisional entries on failure should be ok.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: eng-ml/warmup-experiments -> canary at 21:30 UTC (reminder).

sam: other concern: compatibility with safetensors format. safetensors itself doesn't prescribe chunk checksums but allows custom metadata. We could add a slim extra top-level header (outside tensors) with the fast-open fields. Any objections?

mike: careful — some loaders mmap the file directly and expect offsets. If we insert an extra header, we must keep byte offsets stable or make it optional and advertise via Content-Range/HTTP headers when streaming.

anya: agreed. plan: don't change on-disk shard layout. implement fast-open as external HTTP header (X-Weight-FastOpen: <json-base64>), or as a small sidecar file .fastopen.json alongside shard. both server and object-store-friendly.

tara: that covers streaming. what about signed checksums for provenance? index-hash should be signed by the artifact signer so clients can avoid fetching full manifest for trust.

sam: yep add signature metadata (sig-v1) in the fast-open header. verifies origin before processors accept provisional warmup.

mike: perf note: computing rolling checksums client-side on large streams costs CPU. we might need an opt-in mode per fleet (e.g., "low-trust" vs "fast-verify") and a server-side hint that says whether checksumming is expected.

anya: summary of next steps I propose: 1) prototype .fastopen sidecar + X-Weight-FastOpen header, 2) implement provisional KV entries + tombstone semantics, 3) add signed index-hash workflow + parallel index fetch, 4) measure CPU overhead and have flagging. I'll open a short RFC and a canary experiment tied to infra-bot deploy.

tara: sounds good. can you include a simple header example in the RFC?

anya: sure — example below (base64 of JSON):

```
X-Weight-FastOpen: eyJ2IjoiMSIsImZvcm1hdCI6InNhZmV0ZW5zb3VyY2UiLCJzaGFyZF9zaXplIjoiMjAwMDAwMDAsImNodW5rX2NvdW50IjoiMzIwMCIsImluZGV4X2hhc2giOiJmN2E0ZTgiLCJzaWciOnsiZGIiOiJhbHBoYTEyMyJ9fQ==
```

anya: thanks all — will follow up with RFC link shortly. :thumbsup:
